text: {"claims": [{"id": "c1", "evidence": [{"sid": "P0.S0", "rel": "entails", "sub": "In PostgreSQL versions before 9.4, freezing was implemented by actually replacing a row's insertion XID with FrozenTransactionId"}, {"sid": "P0.S2", "rel": "entails", "sub": "rows with xmin equal to FrozenTransactionId (2)"}], "check": {"kind": "version", "left": "9.3", "op": "<", "right": "9.4"}, "reasoning": "Pre-9.4 freezing replaced xmin with FrozenTransactionId (2); 9.3 is a pre-9.4 version per the version check."}, {"id": "c2", "evidence": [{"sid": "P0.S1", "rel": "entails", "sub": "Newer versions just set a flag bit"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P0.S1 states newer versions just set a flag bit when freezing, matching the claim."}, {"id": "c3", "evidence": [], "check": null, "reasoning": "No sentence mentions WAL volume as a reason; P0.S1 cites forensic use instead, so the claim is unsupported."}, {"id": "c5", "evidence": [{"sid": "P0.S2", "rel": "refutes", "sub": "may still be found in databases pg_upgrade'd from pre-9.4 versions"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P0.S2 says pg_upgrade'd databases may still contain rows with xmin = 2, contradicting 'never'."}, {"id": "c10", "evidence": [{"sid": "P2.S1", "rel": "refutes", "sub": "pg_xact can be expected to grow to about half a gigabyte"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P2.S1 says pg_xact grows to about half a gigabyte at the two-billion maximum, not 2GB (that figure applies to pg_commit_ts)."}, {"id": "c13", "evidence": [{"sid": "P7.S0", "rel": "refutes", "sub": "MXID exhaustion will only block a subset of write transactions"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P7.S0 states MXID exhaustion blocks only a subset, not all write transactions."}]}
